title: One-Hand Form Shooting
description: Shooters release with the shooting hand only, close to the rim, to groove a straight elbow, a wrist snap and a high follow-through without the guide hand interfering.

content.objective: Build a straight, repeatable one-hand release: elbow under the ball, wrist snap, fingers finishing toward the rim.
content.setup: Players one metre in front of the rim, square to it, a ball each; two or three players per basket.
content.organization: Players take turns of five shots, then rotate.
instructions: Balance the ball on the shooting hand's finger pads, wrist bent back, elbow under the ball.
Put the guide hand behind the back.
Bend the knees, extend and push the ball up with one hand.
Hold the follow-through: arm straight, wrist relaxed, fingers pointing at the rim.
Make five, then take one step back; stop at the edge of the lane.
coachingPoints: Elbow under the ball, pointing at the rim.
Ball rolls off the index and middle fingers last.
Hold the finish until the ball hits the rim.
commonMistakes: Elbow flaring out to the side.
Pushing the ball from the palm (flat shot).
Dropping the arm before the ball arrives.
content.safety: Shooters rebound their own ball only when the lane is clear; nobody stands under the rim while others shoot.
progressions: Add the guide hand at the side only for balance.
regressions: Use a smaller ball or a lowered rim.
Shoot at the backboard square only.
variations: Left-hand form shots to build touch.
successCriteria: Five makes in a row at each distance.
content.gameApplication: Every good jump shot is built on the one-hand release; this keeps it clean.
